title: IDF discounts corpus-common terms
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: IDF discounts corpus-common terms. Define: Smoothed IDF is ln((1+N)/(1+df))+1 in this notebook. title: TF-IDF is a fitted representation
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: TF-IDF is a fitted representation. Define: Fit the vectorizer on the frozen corpus; transform questions with it. Walk through: The same query should be scored against one fixed index. New documents require an explicit index version. Ask: What happens to unseen query words? Expected answer and boundary: They do not create new fitted coordinates. A fully out-of-vocabulary query gives a zero vector under this baseline. Visual purpose: show Frozen corpus > Fit vocabulary and IDF > Transform query. title: Cosine compares directions
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Cosine compares directions. Define: Normalize vectors before using their dot product as similarity. Walk through: q=[1,1], d=[2,0]; cosine=2/(sqrt(2)*2)=0.707. Ask: Is cosine a probability that the passage is correct? Expected answer and boundary: No. It is a geometric similarity under the representation. A threshold is an operating rule, not calibrated confidence. Visual purpose: show Dot product / product of norms = cosine. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. title: Thresholds trade coverage and abstention
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Thresholds trade coverage and abstention. Define: Return no evidence when the maximum score is below a declared threshold. Walk through: Use an in-vocabulary protocol question and an unrelated vocabulary question. Inspect full score vectors. Ask: Does a low score prove the answer does not exist? Expected answer and boundary: No. Lexical mismatch can hide a relevant passage. Abstention is a limitation-aware action, not a proof of absence. Visual purpose: show Max score < threshold > Abstain > Ask for evidence.
